raw_response:
Quzhou is on the North China Plain. My family has farmed here for generations. The land is flat, the wells are deep but still working, and the grain station takes wheat every June. I know one system well: winter wheat, then summer maize on the same ground. That is what I will do again.

I have about 10 mu. All of it goes into the rotation — I cannot afford to leave any fallow. Wheat is stable, the government sets a floor price, and the township cooperative handles marketing. Maize feeds the local processors and the price has been decent. Growing vegetables or cotton would mean more labor and more risk. My wife works in the county town now and I manage the farm mostly alone with seasonal help. I cannot take on the complexity.

For wheat I will buy Jimai 22 seed through the village cooperative — it is proven here and partly subsidized. Before planting in mid-October I will apply a compound base fertilizer, then top-dress with urea around the jointing stage in April. I irrigate three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray herbicide in early spring and a combined fungicide-insecticide at heading for scab and aphids. I rotary till after the maize comes off in late September to work the stubble in.

For maize I drill directly into the wheat stubble in mid-June — no tillage, saves time and moisture. I use Xianyu 335 hybrid, which everyone around here grows. Base fertilizer goes down at planting, I top-dress with urea at the big-bell stage. Usually one irrigation in July if the rains are late. I spray herbicide early and check for stem borer around July — one spray if I see it.
